questions.q: What does the summary say happens in the brain of someone who practices mindfulness?
a: The amygdala becomes less active and stress falls
The prefrontal cortex shuts down completely
Gray matter is gradually replaced by white matter
The fight-or-flight response becomes much stronger
questions.why: Lesson 1 says meditation calms the amygdala, the area behind stress and fight-or-flight.

questions.q: What does neuroplasticity mean, according to the summary?
a: The brain's ability to change itself
The brain's store of childhood memories
The mind's refusal to form new habits
The body's physical response to meditation
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes neuroplasticity as the brain's ability to modify itself, which meditation unlocks.

questions.q: What does the summary advise when your mind starts to wander at work?
a: Observe your thoughts without holding on to them
Write every thought down in a notebook
Switch to a more interesting task
Block out all external noise with music
questions.why: Lesson 2 suggests watching thoughts from an outside perspective instead of grabbing hold of them.

questions.q: Why are mindful leaders better at handling challenges?
a: They split problems into manageable parts
They avoid asking others for help
They make decisions faster than anyone
They ignore tension until it passes
questions.why: Lesson 3 says self-awareness lets them see limits, delegate and break challenges down.

questions.q: What effect does a mindful leader have on a company, according to the summary?
a: Employees copy the leader and the whole team improves
Employees compete harder for promotions
The company needs far fewer meetings
The company grows faster than its competitors
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the leader's influence ripples outward as employees try to emulate them.
